members.name: pooled
members.para: Pooled memory: the rows are held in arrays rented from a pool and given back when the call, the buffer or the stream is done. By default that pool is MemoryPool<T>.Shared (backed by ArrayPool<T>.Shared). To use your own, call .UsePool(pool, clear: ...) after Map: the pool is yours, ODX rents from it and gives back to it, and never disposes it. It must hand out whole arrays (MemoryPool<T>.Shared and ArrayPool-based pools do), or the read throws ; it may hand out a larger array than asked for; and its Return must not throw.

Clearing: rows that hold references (a class, a string, a struct that contains either) are always cleared before their array goes back, so a pooled array never keeps a row alive; nothing turns that off. Rows with no references (an int, a plain struct) go back as they are, unless asked: UsePool(pool, clear: true) clears them, clear: false keeps them as they are whatever the app-wide setting says, and a query that does not call UsePool follows the setting. The app-wide setting is the AppContext switch Open.Database.Extensions.ClearPooledArrays (off by default; read once, so set it before the first query). Set it in the project file with <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="Open.Database.Extensions.ClearPooledArrays" Value="true" />, which puts it in runtimeconfig.json, or call AppContext.SetSwitch before the first query.
